reports.title: Zahra Mohamed: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: The MPS will now request a weekly Community Consultation Meeting between AMHPs, MH policing teams, Neighbourhood policing teams, Crisis Teams, and Home Treatment Teams (HTT) to discuss those people who may be reaching the threshold for an assessment/S135 warrant application.
promises.summary: Weekly multi-agency meetings to discuss at-risk individuals before warrant applications

concerns.quote: It was accepted that a s135(2) warrant should have been applied for on 4 October 2022. However, if an application had been submitted to the magistrates' court that day, it is unlikely that the warrant would have been executed before Mrs [name redacted] death. In evidence, I was informed by a number of mental health professionals that the time taken for a s135(2) warrant to be obtained from the magistrates' court and executed by the police was in the region of 2 weeks.

The process for obtaining a warrant is that an application has to be made for a video hearing at either Uxbridge or Westminster Magistrates' Courts. It could take several days for a hearing to be arranged as the courts consider applications from all 32 London Boroughs. Once the Magistrates issued a warrant, an appointment would then be arranged for the police to execute the warrant.
I was informed that a 2-week timescale for obtaining s135(2) warrants was still the case in the summer of 2024.

I also heard evidence that the mental health team could attend Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court in person to apply for a warrant in urgent cases but that they were actively discouraged from using this process by the court.

The court heard that the process and timescale for issuing and executing warrants had led to the hospital team adopting a practice of asking the community team to encourage a patient to return to hospital voluntarily before making an application for a warrant.
concerns.hazard: encouragement of voluntary return instead of warrant

concerns.quote: There is an ongoing risk that patients will harm themselves or others in the period before the warrant can be executed. This includes a risk of fatal harm.
concerns.hazard: risk of self-harm or fatal harm before warrant execution

reports.title: Edward Muwanga: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: A failure by the three police officers attending to understand that their powers under section 136 MHA 1980 applied to persons in a communal space within private accommodation and thereafter a failure to make a more detailed and measured assessment of the Eddie's situation
concerns.hazard: failure to assess mental health crisis in communal space

concerns.quote: A lack of awareness by the two less experienced officers about the process under section 135 MHA 1980, and a lack of inquiry by the more experienced officer as to the existence of such a warrant, together with a concern that it was not clear from the evidence where information about the warrant could be obtained by officers
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness of section 135 MHA 1980 process

concerns.quote: The sharing and visibility of important health care records between medical agencies, (held on multiple platforms by multiple health care agencies) in particular here between the treating Trust (SLAM) and NHS 111, and between the Ambulance Service (not NHS 111) and the treating Trust (SLAM)
